I've been thinking about this idea, and I'd like to hear your thoughts on it!

Problem - I like to view photos online, and I am sure a lot of you like to do so as well. When I see a good photo, such as this or this, I always feel that i) I want to express what think about this photo and how great it is, and ii) I want to see what others are thinking, and whether they agree or disagree with me. However, right now I don't do either because i) I am lazy and I don't want to type comments, especially if someone said the same thing, and ii) I am lazy and I don't want to go through 100+ comments.

Solution - I want to create a tool where people upload photos and it does the following.

1) Instead of commenting, people add 1-liners to the image. A 1-liner should be a short comment/description of the photo (such as great lighting, composition could be better, awesome, etc) which others could upvote on. As a user you will be able to upvote existing 1-liners, or add your own if you disagree with the current ones. This process is easy and anonymous, so you'd likely hear both good and bad comments. I am a developer and use a tool called StackShare, basically, they have this 1-liner commenting system as well, except they use it to review development tools. Here is an example.

2) 1-liners get visualized on a Google map, with pins of different colours or texts. Basically, if you submit a 1-liner, we would display a pin (based on your IP location) to illustrate your location & the comment you submitted. This way, one could look at the map, and easily figure out what the world is saying about this picture. For example, if you post a food picture (e.g. /v/foodpix), you may end up seeing what one part of the world really love your food, while another part really hate. It offers some more insights to what others are saying, both for the OP and for whomever enjoyed/did not enjoy the picture.

An interesting read! While the idea of Liberland intrigued me, as a scholar of Political Science as well as International Relations I knew the idea was destined to fail.

A state with no military whatsoever isn't going to survive in contended territory. It's just being realistic. The international system is one of anarchy, and nobody will defend "Liberland" if Serbia/Croatia decides that it's an infringement on their territory.

The LSA and the Liberland settlers, in my opinion, are confusing "anarchism" with "libertarianism." A libertarian can support having some tax system and central government to overcome collective action problems, such as national defense, road rules, etc. while still supporting minimal government. Anarchism, the complete absence of government, is what "Liberland" currently has.

The best hope of a Libertarian microstate IMO has been the "seasteading" initiatives. The idea behind seasteading is that you essentially build a floating colony (re-purposing an old cruise ship for example), then put it out into international waters. No state really has an incentive to make trouble for the seaborne group, and since it's likely that most of the seasteaders would own weapons pirates wouldn't likely be a serious threat.
